chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would, when he wished to send a commander over a raiding party, order him to have God-consciousness for himself specifically, and then for his companions generally.

Then he would say: 'Go forth in the name of God and fight in the path of God those who disbelieve in God, and do not be treacherous, do not usurp the khums, do not mutilate, do not kill a child, and do not kill a hermit in a high place. Do not burn the palm trees, do not drown them with water, do not cut down a fruit-bearing tree, and do not burn crops, for you do not know, perhaps you will need them. And do not kill animals whose meat is edible, except what you must eat.'
And when you meet the enemy from the polytheists, invite them to one of three things. If they respond to it, accept from them and cease from them.
Invite them to Islam, and cease from them.
And invite them to migration after Islam. If they do so, accept from them and cease from them.
And if they refuse to migrate, and choose their own lands, and refuse to enter into the land of migration, they are like the Bedouin believers; what applies to the Bedouin believers applies to them.
And do not give them any share of the spoils from the distribution, unless they fight in the path of God.
If they refuse these two, invite them to paying the jizya: 'with a willing heart while they are humbled'.
If they give the jizya, accept from them and cease from them. And if they refuse, seek help from God against them and fight them: 'In God, strive his true striving'.

When you besiege the people of a fortress and they want you to accept their surrender based on God's ruling, do not accept their surrender based on God's ruling, but accept their surrender based on my ruling, then judge among them afterward as you wish, for if you accept their surrender based on God's ruling, you do not know whether you have hit upon God's ruling for them or not.

When you besiege the people of a fortress and they want you to accept their surrender under the guarantee of God and the guarantee of His Messenger, do not accept their surrender under the guarantee of God and His Messenger, but accept their surrender under your guarantees and the guarantees of your fathers and your brothers, for if you break your guarantees and the guarantees of your fathers and your brothers, it will be easier for you on the Day of Resurrection than if you break the guarantee of God and the guarantee of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَعْرَاب الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Bedouin believers, referring to a specific legal status regarding spoils.
key_terms.الْجِزْيَة: A tax paid by non-Muslims living under Muslim rule in exchange for protection.
key_terms.تَغُلُّوا: To usurp or take the khums (one-fifth share) prematurely or improperly.
key_terms.تُمَثِّلُوا: To mutilate the bodies of the dead.
key_terms.ذِمَّة: A covenant or guarantee of protection.
key_terms.سَرِيَّةٍ: A small raiding party or military expedition led by a commander.
key_terms.مُتَبِتَلًا: A hermit or monk living in solitude.

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of war and surrender in Shia Islamic jurisprudence according to the Prophet's instructions?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith serves as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence of war (*fiqh al-jihad*), emphasizing that military campaigns are extensions of prophetic instruction rather than mere tactical engagements. It highlights the Prophet’s methodical approach to diplomacy—prioritizing invitation to Islam, then migration, then jizya—while establishing strict ethical constraints on property and non-combatants, reflecting the Shia emphasis on continuity of authority from the Prophet to the Imams.
